summary: self-organization loop: scan -> review -> apply typed ops (proposal queue, never direct edits)
usage: ops organize scan [--dry-run] | review [--accept|--reject|--defer <ids|all>] [--dry-run|--yes] | apply --yes [--safe-only] [--max-ops N] [--max-lines N]
writes: wiki/ (apply only, one git commit per op)
hints: The self-organization loop. scan does ZERO-LLM candidate generation into a typed proposal queue inbox/organize/<date>.jsonl (CLOSED op catalog: add_link, refresh_hub, normalize_tag, fix_frontmatter, retitle, flag_duplicate, propose_merge; validated at write AND read time). A model (OPS_AGENT) only RANKS confidences; with none, heuristics. review appends accept/reject/defer status lines (audit ledger, latest wins) and shows the exact diff each op would produce. apply (needs --yes, NEVER schedulable) deterministically replays APPROVED ops only, one commit per op, with an edit budget (20 ops / 300 lines, flags may only lower it) and protected paths (conventions/index/hubs/pinned) review-only; retitle/propose_merge/deletions never auto-apply. --safe-only applies only the four additive primitives above 0.8. Common mistake: expecting apply to run a model (it never does) or to touch a protected path.
